text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Out-going prime minister, Andris Shkele, announced he is ready to form a new government if supported by President Guntis Ulmannis and the majority of parliament deputies.

- The leaders of the two largest parties, Democratic Party Saimnieks and Latvia's Way, Ziedonis Chevers and Valdis Birkavs, announced after a meeting that they succeeded in smoothing over all the differences between each other.

- Ulmanis wants the three major factions, Fatherland & Freedom, Saimnieks and Latvia's Way to agree on the candidature to the post of the next premier. The three are to hold talks on Saturday, after which they are expected to announce who they want as prime minister.
- Parliament passed amendments to the law on appartment rents, which removes restrictions on the rent imposed by the cabinet of 7.5 santims per square metre).

- Deputies continued to consider the draft law on compulsory motor insurance. Insurance tariffs have been considerably reduced, which made the head of the judicial committee question the implementation of the law.

- The EU Interior and Justice comissioner Anita Gradin and Andris Shkele have signed an agreement which grants Latvia five million Ecu for different purposes including communication, environment protection and the development of infrastructure.
- The president of Riga Commercial Bank, Vladimir Kulik, and a member of Latvia's national chess team, Andrei Sokolov, have been granted citizenship for special merits to this country.
DIENA

- The price of privatisation vouchers has risen by average 0.40 lats over the last two weeks. The increase is explained by the coming privatisation of major state-owned enterprises, with a part of the shares to be sold at public auctions for vouchers.

- The World Bank's permanent representative in the Baltic states, Lars Jeurling, said the three main factors hindering the improvement of the business environment in Latvia are organised crime, corruption and bureaucracy.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The head of the finance ministry's taxation policy department, Arturs Kodolins, resigned and will serve as adviser to the ministry's state secretary, Valentina Andreyeva.
- Last year foreign citizens adopted 195 Latvian-born children.
BIZNES & BALTIJA
- Riga District Court has declared bankrupt the Sloka paper mill, which has debts of 8.8 million lats.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- Compared to a year ago, in December 1996 the average salary of those working in the public sector increased by 18 percent, according to the State Statistics committee. Consumer prices grew by 13 percent.
- Latvian commercial banks had total assets of 1.134 billion lats in December, exceeding for the first time the assets they had before the mid-1995 crisis.
- Wednesday's T-bill auction showed a 0.7 percent to 1.3 percent reduction in average rates of discount of the T-bills. Experts say the reduction is due to Latvia's credit rating.
- Hydro Texaco will open eight new gasoline stations in Latvia on January 24-25.
